title: Titration curve (pH vs. volume of titrant)
body: A titration curve plots pH against the volume of titrant added and summarizes results from a titration; students read it to find the equivalence point and, for weak acids/bases, the half-equivalence point.

items.label: Equivalence point
items.meaning: moles of titrant added equal moles of analyte originally present (monoprotic acids or bases); pH is set by the major species present (neutral for strong acid-strong base; basic for a weak acid titration, acidic for a weak base titration)

items.label: Half-equivalence point
items.meaning: for a weak acid, the point halfway to the equivalence point where [HA] = [A−], so pH = pKa

caution: Do not confuse the half-equivalence point (pH = pKa) with the equivalence point; pKa is read from the pH at the half-equivalence point, not the equivalence point.
ced_evidence: 8.5.A.1 A titration curve, plotting pH against the volume of titrant added; 8.5.A.3 half-equivalence point, pH = pKa

title: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation

items.label: pK_a
items.meaning: negative log of the acid ionization constant K_a of the weak acid (unitless)

items.label: [HA]
items.meaning: concentration of the conjugate acid (weak acid) (mol/L)

caution: Relates buffer pH to the pKa and the concentration ratio of the conjugate acid-base pair. Derivation of the equation and computation of the change in pH on adding acid or base to a buffer are not assessed on the AP Exam.
